findings.recommendation: VMs in this VNet cannot access the remote VNet over the peering even though the peering state can still show Connected. Re-enable virtual network access on this side (compare both sides: the break often looks one-way).
findings.remediation_script:
# Human review required. Read-only verification (the agent never runs writes):
az network vnet peering show -g rg-netops-spoke --vnet-name vnet-spoke1 -n spoke1-to-hub --query "{state:peeringState,sync:peeringSyncLevel,access:allowVirtualNetworkAccess,fwd:allowForwardedTraffic,gwTransit:allowGatewayTransit,remoteGw:useRemoteGateways}"
# Change (review before running):
# az network vnet peering update -g rg-netops-spoke --vnet-name vnet-spoke1 -n spoke1-to-hub --set allowVirtualNetworkAccess=true
findings.title: Peering spoke1-to-hub (vnet-spoke1 -> vnet-hub) has allowVirtualNetworkAccess=false (one-way: the remote side allows access)

reasons: NVA/firewall next hop(s) 10.0.1.4 are in vnet-hub
this side uses the remote gateway

findings.recommendation: Traffic forwarded by an NVA / firewall or gateway in the remote VNet (not originating there) is not accepted over this peering. Enable allowForwardedTraffic on this side.
findings.remediation_script:

# Change (review before running):
# az network vnet peering update -g rg-netops-spoke --vnet-name vnet-spoke1 -n spoke1-to-hub --set allowForwardedTraffic=true
